question: What is the tenant unit, and which isolation profiles are supported at release 1?
recommendation: The tenant is the legal sponsor. Default: one database per legal sponsor on shared managed infrastructure, deployed from one release. Distribution partners of that sponsor get separate schemas inside the sponsor database, which is an approved separate-schema profile. Sponsor-level ledger operations stay atomic because PostgreSQL transactions span schemas in one database. Per-partner schemas need generated Strata projects because Strata has no schema templating (DG-11). Dedicated cells only when a TenantIsolationDecision cites a contractual clause (UNB-RCN-PLT-012). Global holds carry a publication watermark checked at release and dispatch (UNB-RCN-PLT-003). Alternative requiring owner approval: row-level security between partners inside the sponsor database (the not-yet-approved fourth profile, PARTNER-SEGREGATION-AND-TENANCY.md:38; RCC-PLT-009)
alternatives: All three profiles from day one (cost and migration matrix); database per partner (splits sponsor books); single shared database (weakest legal-entity isolation); row-level security between partners (needs owner approval of the fourth profile)
rationale: Database per partner breaks sponsor-level transactions (RCF-PLT-003); one shared database for all sponsors makes cross-legal-entity leakage a single-bug risk; database per sponsor satisfies both and uses Strata's verified multi-database deployment
decided_option: Tenant = legal sponsor. One database per legal sponsor on shared managed PostgreSQL, deployed from one release. Distribution partners get separate schemas inside their sponsor's database. Dedicated cells only on a cited contractual clause. Schema-per-tenant across sponsors and row-level security as a default are both rejected. Global hold watermark adopted.
decision_basis: Keeps each sponsor's books transactional, isolates legal entities physically, and respects the existing owner position against default row-level isolation

question: ACH Notification of Change versus pinned destinations
recommendation: On a NOC, new releases to the old account are held until the destination update is verified. On a charity-requested change, the old account stays live until the new one activates. Payments already authorized keep their destination.
